activities.anchor: the definition has graceful edge cases
activities.caption: run the five tests — file each candidate
activities.name: mineralFiveSort

config.prompt: The five-part definition has teeth — file each candidate:

items.label: coal — no order in its atoms
petroleum — natural but liquid and mixed
opal — natural and solid, but without an ordered lattice (a mineraloid)
a pearl — only organisms can make it
a lab-grown ruby — flawless but not naturally occurring
halite crystallising in an evaporating basin

config.why: Naturally occurring, inorganic, solid, crystalline, definite composition — every test, every time. 'Mineral' is a status the whole definition must earn.

activities.caption: diamond vs graphite — drag the divider
activities.name: mineralPolyCompare

config.prompt: Same element, different arrangement — drag between the two polymorphs:

before.label: Diamond
before.text: Each carbon bonded to four neighbours in a rigid 3-D framework — the hardest natural substance (Mohs 10), an electrical insulator.

after.label: Graphite
after.text: Carbons in flat sheets held to the next sheet by weak forces — it peels onto paper, slides as a lubricant, conducts along its sheets (Mohs 1–2).

config.why: Polymorphs prove arrangement matters as much as recipe — and quartz's pressure-dependent polymorphs even record how deep a rock was buried.

activities.anchor: cooling in seconds freezes none at all
activities.caption: pair each birthplace with its product
activities.name: mineralBirthMatch

config.prompt: Four ways minerals form — pair each with what it builds:

pairs.right: olivine crystallises first (~1,200 °C), quartz last — granite's large grains vs basalt's microscopic ones
halite and gypsum in evaporating basins; cave calcite from dripping water
quartz veins and much of the world's copper, gold and silver
limestone becomes marble; shale's clays become mica — recrystallised, not melted

config.why: Ingredients, favourable conditions and time — the cooling rate sets the crystal size, and water lets the ions travel.

activities.anchor: The whole sequence is also a thermometer
activities.caption: stack the tetrahedron architectures by linkage
activities.name: mineralTetraOrder

config.prompt: One building block, five architectures — order them as linkage increases:
items: Isolated tetrahedra bonded by iron and magnesium — olivine, the upper mantle's mineral
Double chains — amphibole, more oxygen charges to balance
Sheets — the micas, peeling into transparent windows
Frameworks — every oxygen shared: feldspar and the stubborn, weathering-surviving quartz
config.why: Complexity increases with linkage — and Bowen's reaction series orders the same lineup by crystallisation temperature, so a rock's minerals tell its cooling story.

activities.anchor: Every battery and wind turbine starts as one of these
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the valuable minorities
activities.name: mineralOreSpot

config.prompt: One of these non-silicate claims is backwards — click it:
lines: Carbonates — calcite and dolomite — build limestone, marble and most shells; calcite fizzes in dilute acid.
Oxides — hematite and magnetite — are the iron and titanium ores; magnetite is the natural magnet.
Sulfides — pyrite, galena, chalcopyrite — carry copper, lead and zinc.
Gold occurs combined in sulfides, which is why smelting was needed to release it.
Ores are unusual concentrations — hydrothermal veins, banded iron, and lithium evaporated in Andean salars.
config.correction: Gold is a native element — it occurs uncombined, shining in a streambed already pure; that is why it was humanity's first metal.
config.why: Crustal minorities, mighty in value: the classes carry most of the economy even though silicates make up more than 90% of the crust.

activities.anchor: it is worth its own heading
activities.caption: mineral or rock? walk the naming decision
activities.name: mineralRockBranch

config.root: A fresh granite surface sits in front of you. Walk the decision the examiners love to test.

choices.label: A rock — a mixture of minerals
One mineral, called granite
choices.feedback: Granite is an assembly of quartz, feldspar and mica — a mixture, so a rock. No single name is one mineral.

grain.text: Now the parts: glassy grey grains, dull white or pink grains, flaky black specks. What are they individually?

choices.label: Minerals — quartz, feldspar and mica
choices.feedback: Each is one recipe and one lattice — you can learn to point at each on a fresh surface.

choices.label: Three small rocks
choices.feedback: Rocks are mixtures; these are the ingredients themselves — pure substances with definite composition and structure.

done.text: A mineral is one recipe plus one arrangement; a rock is an aggregate you could crush back into its separate minerals — the distinction that separates beginners from students.

wrong.text: The examiners know this trap: when a question asks for a rock, a mineral name is wrong, and vice versa.

rocks3.text: Backwards — the grains are the substances every rock is a sentence built from.

config.why: The relationship is ingredient-to-dish: halite is a mineral, a rock-salt deposit is a rock made of it, and granite is a rock no single mineral name covers.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the field toolkit
activities.name: mineralKitCloze

config.text: A handful of tests narrow 6,000 candidates to one: %%0%% runs from talc (1) to diamond (10), with a copper coin at about 3.5; %%1%% follows the lattice's weak planes — perfect single sheets, or cubes at 90°; %%2%% — the powder colour on unglazed porcelain — is more reliable than the surface colour; and density separates the heavies, galena at 7.5 g/cm³ twice as heavy as quartz.
config.hint: Scratching, breaking, and the colour a specimen leaves behind.

activities.anchor: and a hammer makes short work of one
activities.caption: bet before the reveal — how a diamond is cut
activities.name: mineralHardPredict

config.q: A jeweller must shape a diamond — the hardest natural substance. Which property does the work?
choices: Its hardness — nothing else can abrade it, so lasers finish the job
Its cleavage planes — a sharp split along the lattice's weak links
config.why: Hardness resists scratching; toughness resists cracking — diamond is Mohs 10 yet brittle, and jewellers split it along its cleavage directions. Knowing the cleavage is the practical half of knowing the hardness.
